last_assistant_message:
## System Improvement Opportunities

**Period:** 2026-08-23 to 2026-09-17
**Corrections logged:** 79 (49 explicit, 27 self-detected, 3 unlabeled)
**Severity:** 5 critical, 16 major, 4 high, 33 moderate, 11 minor, 7 medium, 3 other (severity taxonomy is drifting — see Data Hygiene below)

### Recurring Patterns

**assumption-error → wrong-assumption** — 9 occurrences this period (32 all-time, pat-003)
- What keeps happening: agents conclude a capability is unavailable when a lookup fails, instead of verifying through an alternate path. Three distinct sub-cases this period: Master treated `osascript`/Desktop Commander as a missing MCP connector (err-20260826T190920-584QFY, err-20260916T200418-CRJ2R2); Harper aborted a scheduled content-discovery run because ToolSearch returned nothing for a deferred tool (err-20260908T222842-RH9398); Knox ran a Monday-only workflow on a Friday despite a date-conflict signal (err-20260911T154310-IY615I).
- Proposed fix: add a standing rule to SYSTEM.md: *"If a documented capability doesn't surface via ToolSearch, retry once, then check whether it is a Bash/CLI capability before declaring it unavailable. Never abort a scheduled run on a single negative lookup."* Plus a day-of-week gate on day-bound workflows (`date +%A` assertion at entry).
- Fix type: rule + workflow-update. **Recommendation: Apply now** (Tier 1 — the Harper abort fix is already drafted in err-20260908T222842-RH9398's systemic_fix).

**process-skip → protocol-skip** — 7 occurrences (51 all-time, pat-001)
- What keeps happening: two hot sub-threads. (1) The bare-`cd`-before-zip shell-cwd bug bit again (err-20260829T161002-X7JBHO, **major** — this is the 3rd confirmed repeat and already in memory feedback; the fix keeps getting documented but not enforced at the point of execution). (2) Vault-resident files written with the Write tool instead of Obsidian MCP (err-20260907T145247-OMFYBX, major, chase).
- Proposed fix: (1) Move the zip-subshell rule from memory into `skills/git/SKILL.md` / a shell-conventions section of SYSTEM.md so every agent loads it, not just sessions where I recall it. (2) Add to Chase's protocols: any path under `Mind/`, `systems/`, or vault-synced folders must go through Obsidian MCP write tools.
- Fix type: rule + agent-update. **Recommendation: Apply now.**

**tool-misuse → protocol-skip** — 6 occurrences (9 all-time, pat-025)
- What keeps happening: three of the six are the same root cause — eval-harness scripts (`record-step.py`, `guardrail-checkpoint.py`, `new-eval.py`) mistarget eval records because record selection uses name-matching or string-sorted timestamps, silently writing to the wrong run (err-20260911T080849-3TCTQW, err-20260912T080901-GNRQ9D, err-20260827T081312-8HOA70).
- Proposed fix: Rigby capability-build ticket: (1) `new-eval.py` accepts `--name` at creation; (2) record lookup requires explicit `session_id` and fails loudly on no exact match; (3) normalize timestamp precision before sorting. Also patch `systems/dream-cycle/salience-score.py` (os.listdir → os.walk; frontmatter trailing-newline slicing — this bug has now fired 4 times across APAWBB/NBGENM/J571BH/284VH8 and is still unpatched).
- Fix type: skill-update (infrastructure). **Recommendation: Apply now — the salience-score.py patch is fully scoped in err-20260828T081109-J571BH and is overdue.**

**tool-misuse → pattern-mismatch** — 5 occurrences (8 all-time, pat-016)
- Largely the same eval-targeting and salience-score family above. Merged into that fix.

### Agent Performance (this period, normalized casing)

| Agent | Corrections | Top Issue |
|-------|------------|-----------|
| Master | 20 | assumption-error (tool-availability misdiagnosis, cwd assumptions) |
| Jarvis | 13 | tool-misuse (dream-cycle/eval-harness script behavior) |
| Knox | 16 | process-skip (plaud discovery dedup, speaker-ID, artifact updates) |
| Harper | 8 | process-skip (content-discovery abort, duplicate Ghost drafts, missing internal links) |
| Sterling | 4 | data-accuracy (golf booking: wrong cancel button — critical, near-irreversible) |
| Chase | 3 | process-skip (Write tool on vault files) |
| Rigby | 2 | process-skip (research fork exceeded scope and implemented) |

### Tier 2 — Needs Your Call

1. **Sterling golf-booking incident cluster (Sep 4):** a wrong-element click canceled the wrong booking (err-20260914T151500-CANCEL, critical). Browser automation on irreversible actions has no confirmation gate. Do you want a hard rule — *no cancel/delete/refund clicks without a verbal confirm from you* — or a pre-click screenshot-and-verify step in the booking workflow?
2. **Harper content quality cluster (Sep 15):** 3 majors in one run — paraphrase-too-close, missing internal links, wrong-city feature image. This is calibration, not mechanics. Tighten the originality bar in the content skill, or add a pre-publish checklist step?
3. **Severity/category taxonomy drift:** entries are arriving with `medium`/`high`/`critical`/`low` instead of minor/moderate/major, agent names in mixed case (`Master`/`master`), one `failure_mode` containing a 300-char description, and 2 entries with no category at all. Recommend I enforce the schema in `new-entry.py` (reject non-canonical values, lowercase-normalize agent). **Your call** — it's a validator change, zero risk, but it will reject sloppy future writes rather than repair them.

### Trend

Stable-to-improving — monthly volume: Jun 88, Jul 126, Aug 92, Sep 39 (17 days in, pacing ~68). The Aug spike was eval-harness build-out pain; Sep entries skew toward content-pipeline and booking automation, newer surfaces.

### Compaction

No month is currently eligible — every month has open (`proposed`/`in-progress`) entries. 133 proposed fixes are sitting unapplied; that's the bottleneck, not logging.

---

```
--- Eval: rigby-error-analysis (eval-20260901T113710-IMNZVU) ---
Structure 2/4 passed
Failing: rigby-error-analysis output is substantive (>200 bytes), rigby-error-analysis output contains expected content
Deterministic score: 79%  ->  PASS (gate >= 70%)
Tier 3 qualitative grade: pending (runs in tonight's end-of-day sweep)
```

Note on that grade: it ran against a stale Sept 1 eval record, not this run — worth a look at how `grade_skill_run.py` picks its target, given today's pattern findings about record mistargeting are apparently not limited to the dream-cycle.

**Files touched:** `systems/error-tracking/patterns.json` (14 patterns updated, last_analyzed → 2026-09-17), `systems/eval-harness/skill-runs/rigby-error-analysis-latest.json`.

The three Tier 1 fixes are ready to apply on your word: the tool-availability rule, the vault-write rule for Chase, and the salience-score.py/eval-targeting patches.
